messages:
alexander: Heads-up — console alerted to a ~3x bump in schema validation failures for tool calls to `pricing.fetch_price` across canary slice B. Screenshot: https://internal/console/snap/6394321000 :eyes:
opsbot: ALERT: `schema_rejects` metric crossed threshold (5m avg 3.1%). Sample id=6394321000, route=canary-B, region=eu-west-1

maria_g: ugh. is this strict validation rollout hitting production or are these from the permissive sampler?
jen: looks like strict. I see the deploy tag `fncall-strict-2026-03-20` on ~62% of requests in that slice. We only enabled strict on canary-B last night.
samr: quick Q — are these being routed to fallback model variants that don't count against customer quotas? i.e., are we double-billing?
jen: good catch. current flow: strict reject -> client gets structured error -> we route to degen model if fallback policy allows. Quota attribution currently records the final model route only, but billing logs show both attempts in rare cases (race window).

alexander: that's the crux. customer complained about spurious extra tokens and we traced to these rejects + fallback loops. Need a short-term mitigation and a longer-term dashboard/telemetry fix.
maria_g: short-term: disable strict on canary-B or expand permissive sampling for a day. I can flip it. Long-term: we need an explicit 'reject->fallback' trace id in console traces and a discrete metric for 'honor_quota_for_initial_attempt' vs 'final_model_billed'.

jen: proposal for trace metadata: add `fncall_attempts[*].outcome = {"rejected" | "accepted" | "fallback"}` and emit `attempt_index` and `applied_quota_route`. Minimal change in runtime: increment attempt_index when dispatching fallback.
samr: I like that. Also, dashboard: add drilldown for schema error reasons (missing_field, type_mismatch, unexpected_array). Right now console collapses them to "schema_reject" and we can't prioritize which validators are noisy.

alexander: agree. Also need sensible sampling — currently we sample 1% for these rejects which is too small to debug. Can we upsample to 10% for any thread with >50 rejects/min?

jen: yes. I'll add a sampling override tied to alert state. Implementation sketch:
```
if (alerting_rate > 50) { sample_rate = min(0.1, base_rate * 10) }
```
That'll balloon logs but only during incidents.

maria_g: UX note for console: when a strict schema reject happens, the route selector UI should show the rejected payload + validator that failed inline, not buried in raw JSON. That will speed triage.
samr: and we should surface a new quota dimension: `attempt_cost_visibility` which shows token counts for each attempt in the trace waterfall. Right now waterfall only shows the winning attempt.

opsbot: ACTION created: #1234 add reject->fallback trace fields and add attempt-level token accounting (assignee: jen).

alexander: two more edgecases: 1) partially-structured tool responses (array vs object) — sometimes the model wraps an object in an array and our validator rejects; we should attempt a coercion heuristic before strict reject. 2) async toolhooks — we see timeouts happening after a reject and then an async fallback triggers a second attempt, double counting.

jen: for coercion heuristics propose: allow single-element array -> unwrap if schema expects object and element validates. We'll tag the coercion in the trace: `coercion_applied: true` so UX can show it.
maria_g: agree, but make coercion gated by a flag `coerce_singleton_array` per-tool to avoid surprising behavior.
samr: rollout/canary plan: 1) flip canary-B to permissive now (maria), 2) enable attempt-level traces and sample up to 10% for 2 hours (jen), 3) add dashboard row for reject reasons + token-attempts (alex). After data, decide on coercion gating.

alexander: sounds good. maria, can you flip permissive and post confirmation? Also please add a retro note in the rollout board so sales/customer-success hears the mitigation.
maria_g: flipping now. will confirm in 60s. :arrow_forward:
opsbot: deploy: flag `fncall.strict.canary-B` set -> OFF by maria_g (6394321040)
maria_g: done. permissive back on canary-B.

jen: starting work on trace patch. ETA 4h for runtime + 2h for console surface changes. I'll prioritize emitting a compact `attempts` array (but as part of trace blob string) to avoid changing the whole indexer.
samr: when you emit that, add a small numeric code for reason type so dashboards can query across versions (e.g., 1=missing_field,2=type_mismatch,3=unexpected_shape).

alexander: thanks all. after jen's patch and a couple hours of data, we'll reconvene and decide whether to re-enable strict with coercion or expand permissive permanently. Also capture cost impact for any customers that were billed extra.

jen: noted. I'll push a quick sampling dashboard widget (reject-reasons x attempts per minute) while the trace ingestion backend reindexes.
maria_g: leaving a retro note + pinging cs in #customer-success.

samr: if anyone needs a hand with the console query, ping me. I can add a prebuilt time-range linked to the alert that prefilters by route and deploy tag.

alexander: perfect. thanks team. :thumbsup:
